about: CDC CDSi test cases the engine does not pass, with the reason. All are in the underlying-conditions workbook (v4.6, September 2025); every healthy childhood and adult case (v4.46, August 2026) passes. Most were last changed in workbook versions 4.0-4.5 (2016-2023) and encode recommendations or observation codes that differ from Supporting Data 4.65 (August 2026). The test in tests/cdsi_test_cases.rs fails if a case not listed here fails, or if a listed case starts passing. Categories: supporting-data-changed (the expected result reflects earlier ACIP recommendations or series definitions); dose-numbering (the case numbers the forecast dose by counting standard-series doses, while FORECASTDN-1 counts satisfied target doses of the series being forecast); seasonal-dates (the case's assessment date is in an earlier season than the 2025-26 seasonal dates in Supporting Data 4.65); observation-code (the case uses an observation code that is not an indication in Supporting Data 4.65); indication-age (the indication's begin age in Supporting Data 4.65 excludes the patient); series-selection (several risk series are relevant and Chapter 8 scoring selects a different one than the case expects); test-data (the case's inputs conflict with its expected dates); past-due-rule (the expected past-due date omits the one-day subtraction in FORECASTDT-3, which the healthy-suite cases apply). Reasons in the supporting-data-changed category describe the mismatch seen; the earlier supporting-data versions were not retrieved to confirm each change.

exceptions.reason: Observation 079 (encephalopathy after DTaP) contraindicates every pertussis-containing vaccine; in Supporting Data 4.65 those are the only preferable vaccines for Diphtheria/Tetanus dose 2 under 7 years, so Table 7-7 makes the series Contraindicated. The case (v4.0) expects a forecast (DT).
Case v4.0 (PCV7 era): expects dose 1 Valid; the current pneumococcal series evaluate it as Not Valid.

Engine matches status, dose number, earliest, and recommended dates for the health-care-personnel MMR risk series; the case (v4.1) also expects a past-due date (2021-05-27) that the current risk series dose 2 does not define (no latest recommended interval).
Hib risk series for complement deficiency (v4.0): expected earliest date reflects the 2016 series definition.
Hib risk series: the case counts the standard-series dose (expects dose 3); FORECASTDN-1 gives dose 2.

Case name describes a 36-month-old with asplenia but the inputs are a 2-month-old with observation 004 (HSCT); expected earliest (8-week interval) reflects the 2016 series, the current HSCT Hib risk series uses 4 weeks.

Infant MMR travel dose at 6 months completes the infant risk series; the case (v4.0) expects 'Not Complete' with dose 2 at 12 months from the same forecast. The engine forecasts the standard series separately (dose 1 at 12 months, a different vaccine group forecast).
MMR risk series (perinatal HIV, ART): the case counts earlier doses (expects dose 3); FORECASTDN-1 counts satisfied target doses of the risk series (dose 1).
MenACWY risk infant series (v4.2): expected earliest date reflects an earlier interval definition.
MenACWY outbreak infant series (v4.2): expected dates reflect an earlier series definition.

Adult with asplenia: both the 'MenACWY risk 2-23 month' and 'MenACWY risk 2-dose' series are relevant (same priority, no preference); with no valid doses, Table 8-11 scoring (start earliest) selects the 2-23 month series, whose forecast has no minimum age. The case (v4.0) expects the 2-dose series (earliest at age 2 years).
As 2016-UC-0123 (60-year-old, outbreak): the 2-23 month series is selected by scoring; the case expects the series that starts at age 2 years.
Meningococcal outbreak, 60-year-old (v4.0): expected evaluation and 5-year forecast reflect the 2016 series.

The onset-of-pregnancy observation (170) is dated the assessment date, but the expected earliest date (27 weeks after onset) is a year earlier; the expected past-due date also omits FORECASTDT-3's one-day subtraction.
Polio risk adult series after a complete standard series: the case expects dose 5 (counting four standard doses); FORECASTDN-1 gives dose 1.

Polio laboratory worker who already received the additional adult dose (v4.0): the case counts the fifth dose Valid in the risk series; in Supporting Data 4.65 the risk series is satisfied and the dose is Extraneous.
Pneumococcal risk child with cochlear implant (v4.0, PCV13 era): expected evaluation and dates reflect the 2016 series.
Adult pneumococcal risk (v4.5, PCV13/PPSV23 era): expected earliest date uses the 2017 interval; the current series uses 1 year.
Pneumococcal risk child after a complete standard PCV series: the case counts standard doses (expects dose 5); FORECASTDN-1 gives dose 2.
As 2016-UC-0166: the case expects dose 6; FORECASTDN-1 gives dose 2.
Adult pneumococcal risk (v4.1, PCV13/PPSV23 era): expected earliest date uses the 2017 interval; the current series uses 1 year.
Adult pneumococcal risk (v4.5, PCV13/PPSV23 era): expected earliest date uses the earlier interval; the current series uses 1 year.
As 2016-UC-0123 (39-year-old microbiologist and traveler): the 2-23 month series is selected by scoring; the case expects the series that starts at age 2 years.
Cholera (v4.0): expected earliest date uses the former minimum age of 18 years; Supporting Data 4.65 uses 2 years.

MenB 'seeks protection' (observation 177) was a risk series when the case was written (v4.5); it is now the shared-clinical-decision standard series group, where best-series scoring selects the 3-dose MenB-FHbp schedule in which a dose 4 months after dose 1 is valid.
Patient is 8 years 11 months; the dengue indication (observation 211) begins at 9 years, so the risk series is not relevant (Table 5-4). The case expects a forecast at age 9.
As 2022-UC-0001 (8-year-old).

Uses observation 235, which is not an orthopoxvirus indication in Supporting Data 4.65 (indications are 232-234, 236-239, 241-242, 247-248), so no series is relevant.
RSV infant risk series with a 2023 assessment date; the seasonal recommendation in Supporting Data 4.65 starts 2025-10-01, after the patient's maximum age.

Expected past-due date 2025-06-30 is the latest recommended interval date itself; FORECASTDT-3 subtracts one day (2025-06-29), as every healthy-suite HPV case expects.
